issues.description: Removing the outer Delimited drops support for comma-chained ALTER TABLE clauses that the old grammar accepted.
issues.detail: The prior grammar wrapped the OneOf in Delimited(...), accepting e.g. ALTER TABLE t ADD col VARCHAR(20), DROP COLUMN a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS c. The PR removes that fixture and the wrapper, so SQL valid under T-SQL (mixing ADD/DROP/ALTER COLUMN clauses with commas) will now fail to parse. State the invariant explicitly: each ALTER TABLE permits exactly one top-level action. If that is intentional, document it; otherwise this is a regression.

issues.description: IdentityGrammar accepts a stray sign on the increment with no audit of legality.
issues.detail: SignedSegmentGrammar is now optional before both the seed and increment numeric literals. T-SQL allows a negative seed but the increment must be a nonzero signed integer; the grammar invariant should be 'sign optional, magnitude required, increment != 0'. As written, '(+1, -0)' and other oddities parse. Either narrow the grammar or add a literate comment stating the looseness is intentional.

CREATE LOGIN ... DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepts an LCID-like number per MS docs only via sp_configure semantics; allowing a bare numeric literal in the CREATE LOGIN grammar is broader than necessary. A short comment citing the MS reference (or a tighter rule) would meet the literate-programming bar Knuth asks for whenever a grammar surface is widened.

issues.description: Test fixtures cover only the happy path; no negative or boundary cases are added.
issues.detail: New fixtures exercise single straight-line examples. Missing: an ALTER TABLE mixing DROP COLUMN and DROP CONSTRAINT in one statement (does the new shape allow it?); IDENTITY with positive sign, with zero increment; CREATE LOGIN with quoted DEFAULT_DATABASE plus numeric DEFAULT_LANGUAGE. Tests complement proofs; without them, the grammar's actual boundary is unknown.

issues.description: Deleted alter_table fixture loses coverage that should be replaced, not removed.
issues.detail: The removed example 'ALTER TABLE ... ADD column_b ... CONSTRAINT exb_unique UNIQUE, DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c' was a real MS Learn example. If it is no longer valid under the new grammar, that is the regression in issue #1; if it remains valid, the fixture should be kept. Either way, deleting without replacement leaves a coverage hole.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The PR adds four useful T-SQL parser extensions with reasonable fixtures, but the ALTER TABLE refactor changes the grammar's shape from "delimited list of clauses" to "single clause" without stating that invariant or justifying the removal of a previously-passing multi-clause fixture — likely a parse regression for valid T-SQL. The IdentityGrammar widening permits signs on the increment with no narrowing or comment, and DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts a bare numeric without citation. Fixtures are happy-path only. Recommend: restore comma-chained ALTER TABLE support (or document the deliberate restriction), tighten IDENTITY's signed-literal handling, and add negative/boundary fixtures.
